Erin / Helios Ops team —

Thanks again for sharing the Q2 pipeline export. We reviewed the numbers and want to run a short alignment call this afternoon to lock the dedicated capacity runway you asked for and go over the ops playbook (bursting, fallbacks, and SLA gates). Goals for the sync: 
- Confirm Q2 monthly peak concurrent request and sustained tokens/day from your export
- Map those figures to a tentative GPU allocation by week (reserved vs burst)
- Agree on telemetry and SLA signals for automatic fallback (e.g., 95th pct latency > X triggers fallback to A-quantized)

I've attached your exported spreadsheet back for easy reference (Helios_Q2_pipeline_export.xlsx) and a first-pass draft of our runway allocation (runway_allocation_draft_v1.pdf). Can you confirm the peak concurrency column is the canonical figure? If so, I’ll circulate an ops runbook and a short checklist for procurement so finance can budget for the reserved commit.

Proposed time: today 11:30am PT (30 min). If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Rafael

Hi Rafael —

Thanks for the draft. 11:30am PT works for us. Quick clarifications before the call: 
1) "Peak concurrency" on our sheet is the max concurrent sessions at hour granularity — that's what we expect for demo days and product-heavy batch windows.
2) "Sustained tokens/day" is the rolling 7-day average — call that our production baseline.

Two asks for the agenda: can you include an item mapping burst-cost exposure by week (we'd like to see a best/likely/worst cost scenario tied to your suggested reserved commit), and a short section on how you recommend we instrument end-to-end traces for latency SLOs?

FWIW, procurement will want an estimated monthly commit number by Monday to start the PO process.

See you at 11:30.

—Erin

All —

I pulled a quick allocation mapping to bring to the call; notes below so the team can prep: 
- Baseline (sustained tokens/day -> reserved): map 60% of sustained to reserved capacity to keep unit-cost efficient; rest covered via burst slots.
- Peak (concurrent sessions): size GPU pool for 75% of expected peak concurrency to allow for autoscale + 25% burst cushion.
- Week-by-week: proposed ramp for May -> July in the draft (see runway_allocation_draft_v1.pdf).

Risk & mitigations:
- If Helios has overlapping demo-days (2+ in a week) we recommend temporarily increasing reserved commit for that week or pre-purchasing burst credits — procurement note: burst credits invoiced monthly.
- Telemetry: add a lightweight tracing header at the request layer; we can surface 95th percentile downstream in Console. (Marcus will share a short instrumentation checklist.)

Action items for the call: 
1) Rafael: send finalized cost scenarios (best/likely/worst) for committed capacity vs expected burst spend (Erin's ask).
2) Marcus_lin: share instrumentation checklist and Console dashboard template during the call.
3) Helios: confirm whether peak concurrency column is final and flag any demo-day clusters.
